Test prespecified interactions, and report what the test rests on

Source: R/interactions.R
mm_interactions.Rd

Evaluates each candidate interaction as an addition to the project's main-effects model and reports the evidence for it. It returns evidence and nothing else: no model is modified, no term is added, and no interaction reaches a nomogram because a p-value was small. Deciding what the model contains stays with the analyst, which is what makes this a diagnostic rather than a selection procedure.

Usage

mm_interactions(
  project,
  cohort,
  candidates,
  test = c("LR", "Wald"),
  adjustment = c("none", "BH", "holm"),
  nonlinear = NULL,
  knots = 4L
)

Arguments

project

A mm_project().

cohort

The cohort. Its development rows are used, under the same eligibility rule mm_model() fits under, and the digest is checked so the screen cannot run on a different sample from the model.

candidates

List of length-two character vectors naming the blocks to evaluate. Prespecified: this argument is a hypothesis, not a search.

test

"LR" or "Wald".

adjustment

"none", "BH" or "holm".

nonlinear, knots

Passed to mm_model(), because the shape of the model under test decides the degrees of freedom a block costs.

Value

An object of class mm_interaction_screen.

Details

Each candidate is one block tested against one reduced model, the project's main effects. They are therefore length(candidates) separate comparisons and not a sequence: a block is never tested against a model containing another candidate, because that would make the answer depend on the order they were listed in.

What is reported, and what is withheld

A test is reported only for a block that is identifiable, which mm_interaction_rank() establishes from the design matrix before anything is fitted. A block adding no dimension gets NA and a reason, never a p-value: such a block produces a statistic near zero and a p-value near one, which reads as evidence that the interaction is absent when it is evidence of nothing at all.

Sparsity is reported beside the test and never withholds it. A combination carrying no events leaves the design matrix at full rank, so the interaction is estimable and the near-null result describes the sparsity. Refusing the test there would also refuse the cohorts where an interaction is real and small.

The two tests

test = "LR" is a likelihood-ratio test from the difference in deviance between the reduced fit and the fit with the block added, on verifiably the same rows, cross-checked against rms::anova.rms() with test = "LR". Both numbers are returned, and lr_agrees records whether they match, so the claim is checked on every call rather than once in a test file.

test = "Wald" is the joint Wald test of the whole block from rms::anova.rms(), which is several degrees of freedom whenever a categorical or spline term is involved. It is never the test of one dummy coefficient.

Multiplicity, and what it does not fix

adjustment applies stats::p.adjust() across the candidates and the unadjusted value is always kept beside it. An adjusted p-value addresses having looked at several blocks. It does not address choosing a model from the result and then validating it on the same data, which is optimism from selection and needs the selection repeated inside the resampling. That is not in this function.

Examples

cohort <- mm_synthetic_cohort(n = 600, prevalence = 0.15, seed = 1978)
project <- mm_project("uds", "event",
                      c("age", "bmi", "sex", "prior_uti"),
                      positive_class = 1, cohort = cohort)
mm_interactions(project, cohort,
                candidates = list(c("prior_uti", "sex"),
                                  c("age", "bmi")))
#> mm_interactions(): 2 prespecified block(s), LR test, multiplicity none
#> <mm_interaction_screen>  prespecified, LR test
#>   development 600 rows, 95 events, 4 parameter(s) before any block
#>   candidates  2 block(s) considered, 2 parameter(s) of candidate complexity in total
#>   prior_uti x sex        tested  chi2=3.917 df=1 p=0.0478
#>   age x bmi              tested  chi2=0.002 df=1 p=0.9645
#>   Evidence about blocks, not a model. Nothing here has been added to
#>   a model, and a small p-value is not a reason to add it: the
#>   optimism of choosing on these data is not corrected by this
#>   function.
